views.name: dim_academic_terms_current
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  academic_terms.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY,
  academic_terms.TERM_CODE,
  academic_terms.TERM_DESCRIPTION,
  academic_terms.TERM_START_DATE,
  academic_terms.TERM_END_DATE,
  academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC,
  academic_terms.IS_CURRENT_TERM,
  academic_terms.IS_REGULAR_TERM,
  academic_terms.TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR,
  academic_terms.TERM_STATUS,
  academic_terms.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM academic_terms
WHERE (academic_terms.IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'Y' OR academic_terms.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y')

params.description: Current or regular academic term attributes — returns one row per academic term that is marked current or regular.
params.when_to_use: Lookup the current academic term(s) for filtering other datasets (e.g., enrollments, schedules). | Join to fact-level enrollment or event tables to restrict analysis to current/regular terms. | Compose into queries that need term attributes (start/end dates, academic year, status) for reporting or time-based calculations. | Drive UI drop-downs or parameter lists that should show only current or regular terms.
params.output_schema: ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY: surrogate key for the academic_terms row — derives from academic_terms.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY | TERM_CODE: short code/identifier for the term (e.g., '2026A') — derives from academic_terms.TERM_CODE | TERM_DESCRIPTION: human-readable description of the term — derives from academic_terms.TERM_DESCRIPTION | TERM_START_DATE: date when the term begins — derives from academic_terms.TERM_START_DATE | TERM_END_DATE: date when the term ends — derives from academic_terms.TERM_END_DATE | ACADEMIC_YEAR: numeric or coded academic year associated with the term — derives from academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR | ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC: human-readable description of the academic year — derives from academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC | IS_CURRENT_TERM: flag ('Y'/'N') indicating whether this is the current term — derives from academic_terms.IS_CURRENT_TERM | IS_REGULAR_TERM: flag ('Y'/'N') indicating whether this is a regular/standard term — derives from academic_terms.IS_REGULAR_TERM | TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR: short indicator code for status — derives from academic_terms.TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR | TERM_STATUS: textual status for the term — derives from academic_terms.TERM_STATUS | WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE: row load/timestamp for the source row in the warehouse — derives from academic_terms.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.grounded_columns: academic_terms.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY | academic_terms.TERM_CODE | academic_terms.TERM_DESCRIPTION | academic_terms.TERM_START_DATE | academic_terms.TERM_END_DATE | academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR | academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC | academic_terms.IS_CURRENT_TERM | academic_terms.IS_REGULAR_TERM | academic_terms.TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR | academic_terms.TERM_STATUS | academic_terms.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact tables (e.g., enrollment, grades, schedules) on academic_terms.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY or TERM_CODE — safe because this view is one-row-per (ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY, TERM_CODE) and contains only descriptive attributes (no aggregated measures) so joining will not duplicate pre-aggregated metrics from this view itself. | Safe to join to other dimension tables that are also one-row-per-key (for example, a departments or subjects dimension keyed by their own surrogate keys) as long as joins are on those keys and maintain one-to-one semantics. | Do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many child tables (for example: class sections, weekly enrollment breakdowns, student-level enrollments) if you intend to preserve the cardinality of those child measures unless you are joining for filtering only or you re-aggregate after the join. Joining one-to-many tables without aggregation will multiply result rows and will duplicate any measures computed before the join. | If you need to combine this view with sibling aggregated views (e.g., agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept) ensure the join keys match the aggregation grain. For example, join dim_academic_terms_current.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY = agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY — this is safe provided agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept is already aggregated at that term key (it will not multiply aggregated measures). | When composing further aggregates: (a) treat all columns here as attributes/dimensions, not measures; (b) if you join a one-to-many fact to this view and then aggregate, compute measures from the fact after the join (e.g., SUM(fact.enrolled_students) GROUP BY dim_academic_terms_current.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY). | Because the view filters WHERE IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'Y' OR IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y', verify that downstream joins/filters account for this subset (it does not represent the full academic_terms domain). If you need all terms, join directly to the academic_terms base table instead.

views.description: One-row-per-term dimension filtered to currently-active or regular academic terms. Useful as a canonical set of terms for joins, calendars, or term-level reporting. | Use for: List active/regular academic terms; Join term-level metrics to the current/regular term set; Filter course sections to current or regular terms

views.name: agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  subject_offered.TERM_CODE,
  subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
  SUM(COALESCE(subject_offered.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) AS total_subject_enrollment_number,
  SUM(COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0)) AS total_num_enrolled_students
FROM subject_offered
GROUP BY
  subject_offered.TERM_CODE,
  subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_NAME

params.description: Aggregated counts of subject enrollments and enrolled students by academic term and offering department.
params.when_to_use: Get total subject enrollment numbers and total enrolled student counts for a given TERM_CODE and OFFER_DEPT_CODE (or OFFER_DEPT_NAME). | Build dashboards or reports that compare department-level enrollment across terms. | Compose higher-level aggregates (e.g., college or campus) by safely rolling up these department-by-term totals. | Filter or join department-term enrollment totals into analyses that need enrollment totals per department per term (e.g., course capacity / utilization, trend lines).
params.output_schema: TERM_CODE: the academic term code for the aggregation; derived directly from subject_offered.TERM_CODE | OFFER_DEPT_CODE: the department code offering the subjects in this aggregation; derived directly from subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_CODE | OFFER_DEPT_NAME: the department name for the offering department; derived directly from subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_NAME | total_subject_enrollment_number: sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER for all subject_offered rows in the same TERM_CODE + OFFER_DEPT_CODE + OFFER_DEPT_NAME group; derived as SUM(COALESCE(subject_offered.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) | total_num_enrolled_students: sum of NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS for all subject_offered rows in the same TERM_CODE + OFFER_DEPT_CODE + OFFER_DEPT_NAME group; derived as SUM(COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0))
params.metric: total_subject_enrollment_number = SUM(COALESCE(subject_offered.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) grouped by (subject_offered.TERM_CODE, subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_NAME) | total_num_enrolled_students = SUM(COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0)) grouped by (subject_offered.TERM_CODE, subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_NAME)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional (one-row-per-key) views/tables on TERM_CODE or OFFER_DEPT_CODE, e.g. join to dim_academic_terms_current on TERM_CODE — safe because dim_academic_terms_current is expected to be one row per TERM_CODE so this AGG's measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a department dimension table (one-row-per-OFFER_DEPT_CODE) on OFFER_DEPT_CODE — safe because the join preserves one row per (TERM_CODE,OFFER_DEPT_CODE) in this view and will not multiply measures. | unsafe join warning: do NOT join directly to any one-to-many child/detail table or view (for example, a raw subject_offered detail or any reshaped detail that has multiple rows per subject or section) without re-aggregating, because those joins will multiply total_subject_enrollment_number and total_num_enrolled_students. If you must join to a one-to-many table, either (a) join on keys and then re-aggregate SUM(...) grouped back to TERM_CODE + OFFER_DEPT_CODE, or (b) first aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per TERM_CODE+OFFER_DEPT_CODE before joining. | unsafe join warning: do NOT join this AGG to sibling aggregated views that are at a finer grain (e.g., enrollment by week or by section) without aligning grain; instead roll the finer-grain view up to TERM_CODE + OFFER_DEPT_CODE before joining to avoid double-counting. | example safe composition for roll-up: to compute college-level totals, join this view to a department->college mapping (one row per OFFER_DEPT_CODE) and then SUM(total_subject_enrollment_number) GROUP BY TERM_CODE + college_id. This is safe because the mapping is one-to-one on OFFER_DEPT_CODE. | example unsafe composition: joining agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept to reshape_subject_enrollment_by_week_flags (which may have multiple week rows per subject) on TERM_CODE and OFFER_DEPT_CODE would duplicate measures unless reshape_subject_enrollment_by_week_flags is first aggregated to the same TERM_CODE+OFFER_DEPT_CODE grain.

views.description: Aggregated enrollment totals per TERM_CODE and OFFER_DEPT_CODE using subject_offered summary numbers. Useful for department-term enrollment trends and rollups. | Use for: Department-level enrollment by term; Trend of enrolled students per department over terms; Compare subject enrollment counts vs enrolled students

views.name: rank_latest_fclt_building_by_key
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
  fclt_building.BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fclt_building.BUILDING_NAME,
  fclt_building.ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  fclt_building.EXT_GROSS_AREA,
  fclt_building.SITE,
  fclt_building.CAMPUS_SECTOR,
  fclt_building.LATITUDE_WGS,
  fclt_building.LONGITUDE_WGS,
  fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  RANK() OVER (
    PARTITION BY fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
    ORDER BY (fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE IS NULL), fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE DESC
  ) AS row_rank
FROM fclt_building

params.description: Provides the latest (ranked) warehouse-loaded snapshot of facility building attributes per building key.
params.when_to_use: Look up current/latest building attributes (name, numbers, areas, location) for a given FCLT_BUILDING_KEY. | Filter facility/building-level analytics to the most recent warehouse load per building before joining to other datasets. | Compose building attributes into reporting or aggregations where one row per building (latest snapshot) is required.
params.output_schema: FCLT_BUILDING_KEY: unique identifier of the facility building — derived directly from fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY | BUILDING_NUMBER: business/building number label — derived from fclt_building.BUILDING_NUMBER | BUILDING_NAME: descriptive name of the building — derived from fclt_building.BUILDING_NAME | ASSIGNABLE_AREA: assignable area metric (units as stored) for the building — derived from fclt_building.ASSIGNABLE_AREA | EXT_GROSS_AREA: gross area metric (units as stored) for the building — derived from fclt_building.EXT_GROSS_AREA | SITE: site code or identifier where the building sits — derived from fclt_building.SITE | CAMPUS_SECTOR: campus sector classification of the building — derived from fclt_building.CAMPUS_SECTOR | LATITUDE_WGS: latitude (WGS) coordinate of the building — derived from fclt_building.LATITUDE_WGS | LONGITUDE_WGS: longitude (WGS) coordinate of the building — derived from fclt_building.LONGITUDE_WGS | WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE: the warehouse load timestamp/date for the row — derived from fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE | row_rank: integer rank (1 = latest non-null WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE per FCLT_BUILDING_KEY) computed by RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY (WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE IS NULL), WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE DESC)
params.grounded_columns: fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY | fclt_building.BUILDING_NUMBER | fclt_building.BUILDING_NAME | fclt_building.ASSIGNABLE_AREA | fclt_building.EXT_GROSS_AREA | fclt_building.SITE | fclt_building.CAMPUS_SECTOR | fclt_building.LATITUDE_WGS | fclt_building.LONGITUDE_WGS | fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.metric: row_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY (fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE IS NULL), fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE DESC) | Note: There are no aggregated metrics (SUM/COUNT) in this view; ASSIGNABLE_AREA and EXT_GROSS_AREA are passed through as stored values from the base table.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension views/tables that are one-row-per-FCLT_BUILDING_KEY (or keyed by the same building key) — e.g., if there is a canonical building dimension keyed by FCLT_BUILDING_KEY — join on fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = dim_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY. This is safe because rank_latest_fclt_building_by_key produces at most one row per FCLT_BUILDING_KEY when you filter to row_rank = 1, so its measures/attributes will not be duplicated. | To ensure one-row-per-building semantics, always filter this view to the latest snapshot per building: WHERE row_rank = 1. Without that filter the view can contain multiple ranks per FCLT_BUILDING_KEY and joining will multiply rows. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., room-level inventories, weekly time series, enrollment facts, or other transactional detail keyed to building) without either: |   - aggregating the one-to-many side to one row per FCLT_BUILDING_KEY before joining, or |   - performing the join and then re-aggregating back to the desired grain. | Examples of unsafe joins (would duplicate/scale ATTRIBUTES incorrectly): join to win_running_room_area_by_building or any room-level table that contains multiple rows per building. Instead aggregate room area by FCLT_BUILDING_KEY (SUM) first, then join to this view. | Safe joins: join to other one-row-per-building views/tables (or other dimensions keyed 1:1 to FCLT_BUILDING_KEY) — safe because this view (when filtered to row_rank = 1) is one-row-per-FCLT_BUILDING_KEY and will not duplicate measures. | When composing metrics that sum areas or counts, prefer this pattern: (1) select row_rank = 1 from this view to get one row per building, (2) join to aggregated fact(s) at building grain or (3) aggregate after join. This preserves correct cardinality and prevents double-counting.

views.description: Window-ranked rows of fclt_building by FCLT_BUILDING_KEY with latest WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE first. Exposes row_rank so downstream queries can select latest per building (rank = 1). | Use for: Select latest building attributes per building; Time-based comparisons of building snapshots; Join latest building rows to rooms or floors

views.name: win_running_room_area_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY,
  fac_rooms.FLOOR,
  fac_rooms.ROOM,
  fac_rooms.AREA,
  fac_rooms.ROOM_FULL_NAME,
  SUM(COALESCE(fac_rooms.AREA, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fac_rooms.ROOM ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_area
FROM fac_rooms

params.description: Provides per-room building-level running sum of room AREA ordered by ROOM within each BUILDING_KEY (cumulative area by room in a building).
params.when_to_use: Show cumulative area by room within a building (e.g., cumulative sqft as you list rooms). | Compose queries that need per-room AREA plus a building-scoped running total ordered by room. | Produce floor or building rollups while preserving the original room-level detail (can be re-aggregated). | Build reports that rank or plot cumulative area growth across rooms in a building.
params.output_schema: BUILDING_KEY: building identifier, derived directly from fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY | FLOOR: room floor identifier, derived directly from fac_rooms.FLOOR | ROOM: room identifier, derived directly from fac_rooms.ROOM | AREA: room area numeric measure, derived directly from fac_rooms.AREA | ROOM_FULL_NAME: descriptive room name, derived directly from fac_rooms.ROOM_FULL_NAME | running_area: cumulative sum of AREA partitioned by BUILDING_KEY and ordered by ROOM; defined as SUM(COALESCE(fac_rooms.AREA, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fac_rooms.ROOM ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
params.metric: running_area = SUM(COALESCE(fac_rooms.AREA, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fac_rooms.ROOM ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)  -- cumulative (running) total of AREA within each BUILDING_KEY ordered by ROOM | AREA (base measure) = fac_rooms.AREA -- used as the atom for the running_area calculation
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension lookups that are one-row-per-BUILDING_KEY (for example, a building-level dimension) on fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY — safe because this view is one-row-per-(FAC_ROOM_KEY/ROOM) and joining to one-row-per-BUILDING_KEY will not duplicate rows or the running_area measure. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tables or views that are one-row-per-ROOM (or keyed by the same ROOM identifier and BUILDING_KEY) on (BUILDING_KEY, ROOM) — safe because it aligns row-for-row with this view's grain and does not duplicate measures. | NOT safe without care: do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables or views keyed at a lower grain (for example, a table containing multiple assets, bookings, or events per ROOM) unless you first aggregate those tables to the room/building granularity or re-aggregate this view's measures after the join — such joins will multiply rows and thus inflate running_area/AREA. | NOT safe without re-aggregation: joining to sibling aggregate views that are many-per-BUILDING_KEY (for example, an aggregation by department that lists multiple rows per building) will duplicate this view's rows unless you aggregate the other side to one row per BUILDING_KEY (or join on a stricter key such as ROOM when available). | If you need building-level totals (not cumulative per-room), re-aggregate this view by BUILDING_KEY using SUM(AREA) and ignore running_area (or compute MAX(running_area) per BUILDING_KEY if you want the total cumulative at the last room in ordering). | When composing joins, prefer equality joins on the exact columns present (fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY, fac_rooms.ROOM, fac_rooms.FLOOR) and treat running_area as a derived, row-level metric that should not be summed across arbitrary many-to-one expansions without explicit re-aggregation.

views.description: Running cumulative area per BUILDING_KEY ordered by ROOM (or ROOM identifier) within fac_rooms. Useful to compute cumulative area distributions within a building or to find rank-by-cumulative-area. | Use for: Cumulative area within a building; Identify smallest set of rooms reaching X sqft (downstream filter on running_area); Distribution of area by room order

views.name: reshape_subject_enrollment_by_week_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  subject_summary.TERM_CODE,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_1ST_CREDIT,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_5TH_CREDIT
FROM subject_summary

params.description: Provides per-subject enrollment counts and credit-weighted enrollments for the first and fifth weeks of a term (one row per SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY / TERM_CODE / SUBJECT_ID).
params.when_to_use: Report subject-level enrollment counts at week 1 or week 5 for a given term or set of terms | Compare early-term (week 1) vs later (week 5) subject enrollments or credits | Build higher-level aggregations (department, term) by summing these subject-level measures | Filter or join subject metadata (title, id) while preserving per-subject enrollment metrics
params.output_schema: TERM_CODE: academic term code for the record — derived directly from subject_summary.TERM_CODE | SUBJECT_ID: subject identifier (e.g., department/subject code) — derived directly from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID | SUBJECT_TITLE: human readable title for the subject — derived directly from subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK: headcount enrollment for the subject in the first week of the term — derived directly from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK: headcount enrollment for the subject in the fifth week of the term — derived directly from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_1ST_CREDIT: credit-weighted enrollment for the subject in the first week — derived directly from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_1ST_CREDIT | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_5TH_CREDIT: credit-weighted enrollment for the subject in the fifth week — derived directly from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_5TH_CREDIT
params.metric: SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK = direct column subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK (interpreted as subject-level headcount at week 1) | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK = direct column subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK (interpreted as subject-level headcount at week 5) | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_1ST_CREDIT = direct column subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_1ST_CREDIT (interpreted as credit-weighted enrollment at week 1 for the subject) | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_5TH_CREDIT = direct column subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_5TH_CREDIT (interpreted as credit-weighted enrollment at week 5 for the subject)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to dim_academic_terms_current on TERM_CODE = TERM_CODE — safe because dim_academic_terms_current is dimensional (one row per term) and does not duplicate subject-level measures | cardinality-SAFE: join to any table that is one-row-per-SUBJECT_ID-per-TERM_CODE (for example, another subject-level dimension keyed by TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID) — safe because keys align to this view's grain and will not duplicate its measures | NOT safe without re-aggregation: do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail tables (e.g., enrollment_detail, class_section, student_term_rows) that have multiple rows per subject per term without aggregating those detail rows to the same grain first, because joining them directly would multiply this view's rows and therefore double-count SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_* and SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_*_CREDIT measures | NOT safe without care: do NOT join to sibling aggregated views that roll up to a different grain (for example, a section-level or student-level aggregated view) unless you aggregate those siblings to SUBJECT_ID+TERM_CODE before joining, otherwise the planner must re-aggregate to avoid duplication | guidance for building on this view: treat the view as one-row-per (TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID). When composing, either (a) aggregate additional detail to that same key and then join, or (b) join only to dimension tables that are 1:1 to that key. If you need finer-grain detail, join and then re-aggregate, ensuring you use SUM(...) over the underlying numeric columns (the SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_* fields) only after grouping back to TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID to preserve correct totals.

views.description: Pivot-like projection exposing first-week and fifth-week enrollment counts side-by-side from subject_summary for easier comparison. Useful for retention/drop analysis between weeks. | Use for: Compare first-week vs fifth-week enrollment; Compute retention rates between weeks (downstream derived ratio); Identify courses with large drop between weeks
